body: OBSERVED at runtime, 2026-08-23, against a container on the pre-fix `:dev` image, with the SAME task visible in both UIs at the same moment. `taskMessage` is deliberately server-built HTML: `cps/helper.py:518` composes `'{}'.format(book_id, escape(book.title))` — the title is escaped there, so this is not an injection hole, it is a rendering-contract mismatch. Classic consumes it as HTML (bootstrap-table's default formatter) and shows a working link. The SPA interpolates the same string as JSX text — `frontend/src/pages/Tasks.tsx:47`, `{task.taskMessage}` — so React escapes it and the user is shown the markup. Rendered accessibility trees, same instance, same task: /app/tasks cell "E-mail: The Enchanted April send to eReader" /tasks cell: text "E-mail:" + link "The Enchanted April" -> /book/197 + text "send to eReader" Do NOT fix this with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Two reasons: it makes the SPA trust server-composed markup for a field that interpolates library data, and the embedded href is a CLASSIC route (`/book/197`), so an SPA that rendered it as HTML would navigate the user out of the SPA — which is precisely what retiring classic is supposed to stop. Fix shape: give `/api/v1/tasks` the structured pieces (message text plus an optional book id) so the SPA composes its own ``, and leave the HTML field for classic.
title: New UI Tasks renders the server's HTML task message as literal text
